summary: Read-only: audit every fp64/parity oracle — does it INDEPENDENTLY encode the canonical algorithm, or MIRROR the kernel (co-wrong, gate-blind like SG11)? Cost-calibrated; adversarially verify co-wrongness
logs: 11 co-wrongness candidates across 5 oracle groups; verifying (opus).

co_wrong_oracles.oracle: tests/hw/sg2_kernel_mirror.py::oracle_step (lines 356-391) — the B1 truth source for the SG2 CSA lightning-indexer top-k, consumed by tests/hw/_sg2_l3tc_gate.py::run_sg2_gate (B1 anchor, lines 168-288, tol 1e-5).
co_wrong_oracles.problem: oracle_step re-implements the KERNEL's low-rank indexer path, not the canonical algorithm — so kernel==oracle by construction for the CSA top-k. CONFIRMED three-way: (1) CANONICAL is FULL-RANK: supergrok2.py:449-450 `qI = (x @ idx_DQ) @ idx_UQ` -> [N,d], `idx_scores = (qI @ c_kI.T)/sqrt(d)`; supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h:156-159 `f.qI = mm(mm(x,idx_DQ),idx_UQ)` [N,d], `/sqrt_d`. (2) KERNEL is LOW-RANK: supergrok2.h:206 `I[t,s]=qI·kI/sqrt(rank)`, qI kept rank-INDEXER_RANK, supergrok2.h:510-511 `(void)idx_UQ` (lift-back explicitly NOT applied to the score). (3) ORACLE mirrors the KERNEL: sg2_kernel_mirror.py:356-361 `qI = x_sorted @ idx_DQ` -> [N,rk] (idx_UQ DROPPED); line 372/381 `inv_rk = 1/sqrt(rk)` (NOT /sqrt(d)). So B1 cannot distinguish a correct low-rank indexer from a buggy one consistent with the mirror. The --selftest (sg2_kernel_mirror.py:905-990) only toggles _USE_VECTORIZED scalar-vs-vectorized of the SAME oracle_step (a vectorization-equivalence check, lines 53/57), and the independent fp64 anchor csa_hca_step_one is itself the low-rank kernel path — neither gives the CSA top-k the independent-algorithm validation that HCA/GRU/PEER/Adam-tail paths get. The N>64 CSA fidelity probe in _sg2_l3tc_gate.py:320-333 surfaces exactly this kernel-low-rank-vs-canonical-full-rank divergence but only `print`s it under `if verbose`, sets no _ok flag; the gate verdict is `ok = b1_ok and aaa_ok and tie_ok` (line 335) so a CSA-indexer regression consistent with the low-rank mirror passes silently.
co_wrong_oracles.fix: Make B1's CSA-indexer reference independent of the kernel's low-rank reimplementation. Option A (preferred): in oracle_step compute the indexer top-k via the CANONICAL full-rank path — qI = (x @ idx_DQ) @ idx_UQ ([N,d]), idx_scores = qI·c_kI / sqrt(d) per supergrok2.py:449-450 / supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h:156-159 — and assert the kernel's selected top-k indices match it; if the kernel is intentionally low-rank, gate the DIVERGENCE with an explicit expected-set/tolerance rather than mirroring the kernel. Option B: add a dedicated independent fp64 full-rank CSA-indexer oracle (derived from the canonical source, NOT from csa_hca_step_one) into the --selftest cross-check so the CSA top-k gets the same independent validation as HCA/GRU/PEER/Adam-tail. Either way, the N>64 fidelity probe (_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:320-333) must set an _ok flag that participates in `ok = b1_ok and aaa_ok and tie_ok` under a justified tolerance, instead of printing only under `if verbose`. Note: the supergrok2 entry in scripts/optimizer_math_manifest.json is only a source hash, not a per-equation spec, so the anchor must be taken directly from supergrok2.py / supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h.
co_wrong_oracles.gate_blind_class: SG2 CSA lightning-indexer top-k selection bugs: any error in the indexer projection / score / top-k selection that is consistent with the low-rank reimplementation (e.g. wrong idx_DQ contraction dim, wrong score normalization, top-k ordering/tie bug) — kernel==oracle by construction, and the only instrument that would catch full-rank divergence (N>64 fidelity probe) is non-voting.

co_wrong_oracles.oracle: tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py — the production per-cell L3-TC gate as actually run by CI: `pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -m hw` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:1352-1353). The only collected test is test_l3tc_cell_gate (line 1460), which runs the COLD step-1 path (sg11_warmup_state=None).
co_wrong_oracles.problem: COVERAGE/LIVENESS blindness to the SG11 cos-operand regression class on the CI path (NOT a kernel==oracle mirror — the fix is encoded correctly; the discriminating instrument simply never runs in CI). The SG11 bug class is the kernel computing cos(grad, MU) instead of canonical cos(grad, MOMENTUM) (supergrok11.h:22-29,72-84; historical fix .perf/sg11_gate_fix.diff). At cold step 1 the cold reference hard-pins the gate: m0 = zeros when ws is None (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:793), so `num=(gt*m0).sum()=0` -> `cos_t=0` -> `gate_t = sigmoid(0) = 0.5` (lines 800-803), fixed unconditionally and never recovering the kernel's actual gate. With default rescale=0.1 the gate-dependent surfaces (params, m/v) are damped below param_tol=1e-4 by Adam v-normalization — the authors' own comments (lines 910-915, 956-957) state a wrong gate diverging by ~0.8 is washed out below tolerance. The discriminating teeth (run_sg11_warmup_gate, lines 882-1059: warms momentum nonzero, gate_div>1e-4 assert line 1054, err_vs_momentum<1e-2 AND err_vs_mu>1e-1 line 1013, rescale pumped to 2.0) are reachable ONLY via the --sg11-warmup CLI flag (line 1479); pytest never calls main(), and grep confirms no Makefile/CI/script passes --sg11-warmup. The docstring-referenced test_sg11_gate_warmup_catches_momentum_bug (line 691) has NO definition. The other named oracle, test_opt_stages.py::test_sg11_cosine_gate_matches_fp64_oracle, never drives the kernel (Python-mirror vs Python-oracle only).
co_wrong_oracles.fix: Promote the warm-up gate to a pytest-collected, CI-run test so the cos-operand class is regression-guarded on the default path: add a `def test_sg11_gate_warmup_catches_momentum_bug` (the name the docstring at line 691 already advertises) that invokes run_sg11_warmup_gate for the SG11 cell with nonzero warmed momentum and rescale pumped (>=2.0), asserting gate_div>1e-4, err_vs_momentum<1e-2, and err_vs_mu>1e-1 — so it is collected by `pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -m hw` without needing the --sg11-warmup CLI flag. Equivalently, have CI run main() with --sg11-warmup. The cold step-1 path alone must not be the sole CI guard for SG11 since its gate is structurally pinned to 0.5 and its gate-dependent surfaces are sub-tolerance at the default rescale.
co_wrong_oracles.gate_blind_class: SG11 cos-operand regression — kernel reading the just-written mu_blob (cos(grad,mu)) instead of the start-of-step exp_avg (cos(grad,momentum)) as the 2nd cosine operand, and more broadly any gate-magnitude error whose effect on params/m/v is damped below param_tol=1e-4 at the cold step's small rescale. The exact SG11 incident class is unguarded on the CI path.

co_wrong_oracles.problem: LATENT SG11-class co-wrong SHAPE (currently the operand is correct, but nothing pins it): _sg11_gate_oracle_fp64 is a LOCAL re-implementation, not a canonical import, computing the IDENTICAL expression to the kernel-side twin _sg11_gate_mirror_fp32 (num=Σg·m, den_g=Σg·g, den_m=Σm·m, sigmoid(temp·num/sqrt(den_g·den_m+1e-12))); the ONLY differences are fp64-vs-fp32 and naive-sum-vs-block-tree. The cosine's 2nd operand is hardcoded `momentum` in BOTH twins and nothing external pins it. No imported reference encodes the operand: the canonical ref_sg11_step (test_reference_parity.py:189-199) takes `gate` as a PRE-REDUCED SCALAR INPUT (signature `*, gate`), so it cannot anchor the operand; its docstring points at sg11_gate_ref and parity_gate_h100._cosine_gate_ref, but a repo-wide grep finds NO definition of either (they are phantom references, test_reference_parity.py:193); and the genuinely canonical cosine sg11_finalize_gate (supergrok11.h:72-84) is C++ and not imported. So a co-edit that swapped BOTH twins to cos(grad,mu) would pass test_sg11_cosine_gate_matches_fp64_oracle cleanly — the exact SG11 two-same-file-twins failure shape. The in-file teeth (test_sg11_gate_applies_gate_temp, test_sg11_gate_is_per_tensor) anchor temperature-consumption and per-tensor independence, NOT operand identity.
co_wrong_oracles.fix: Give _sg11_gate_oracle_fp64 an operand anchor independent of the kernel mirror. Option (a) preferred and robust (since the phantom refs don't exist): add a closed-form case where cos(grad,momentum) != cos(grad,mu) — construct grad, a momentum vector, and a DISTINCT mu vector, hand-compute the expected sigmoid(gate_temp·cos(grad,momentum)) from a literal, and assert the oracle equals it AND differs from sigmoid(gate_temp·cos(grad,mu)) — so a co-edit swapping the operand to mu fails here. Option (b): pin the operand from a single non-twin source — import/adapt test_l3tc_tail_gate.py's independent cos(grad,m0) construction (lines 800-803) or create a real shared sg11_gate_ref — rather than re-deriving locally; ideally validate the staged mirror against sg11_finalize_gate (supergrok11.h) semantics rather than a same-file fp64 copy.
co_wrong_oracles.gate_blind_class: SG11 cos-operand swap (cos(grad,momentum) -> cos(grad,mu)) introduced by a co-edit touching both same-file twins; more generally any change to the cosine's operand identity, which the fp64/fp32 + tree/naive differences cannot catch.

trustworthy: The ref_<opt>_step canonical fp64 set in tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py (ref_adamw/lion/grokadamw/grokfast/neuralgrok/looksam/prodigy/sg11/sg15/sg2/muon_step + helpers ref_sg_phi_forward/ref_neuralgrok_psi_forward/ref_prodigy_partials/ref_looksam_set_direction). Each is an INDEPENDENT transcription of the per-element math in csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (verified line-for-line: e.g. ref_sg11 smart_grad=g+(1-gate)*alpha*mu == supergrok11.h:130; ref_muon NS a/b/c=3.4445/-4.7750/2.0315, scale=0.2*sqrt(max(rows,cols)) == muon.h+bindings.cpp). The CPU self-consistency tests derive expected values from first principles independent of any kernel. The SG11 co-wrong risk does NOT live inside the refs — they take gate/mu/sam_dir/momentum as caller-supplied inputs; the risk is purely in how the GATE CALLER computes those args, which is the subject of the three confirmed findings.

The four model fp64 reference oracles — tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py, vit_oracle.py, mamba_oracle.py, mamba3_oracle.py — each encode the algorithm from first principles (primitive PyTorch ops, hand-derived backward validated against torch.autograd) and none read cached intermediates written by the CUDA kernel. The SG11 co-wrong class (oracle re-reads the buffer the kernel writes instead of recomputing from canonical inputs) is not present. These are out-of-band for the optimizer cos-operand class.

The decoder and vit kernel mirrors (tests/hw/decoder_kernel_mirror.py, vit_kernel_mirror.py) independently encode the algorithm and recompute their own intermediates (have _recompute_layer); they are not co-wrong with the kernel for mirror-vs-oracle comparison. The sg2_kernel_mirror.py mirror_step path (as distinct from oracle_step) is genuinely independent of oracle_step for the non-CSA-indexer surfaces (HCA/GRU/PEER/attention/Adam-tail are cross-checked).

The mamba kernel mirror (tests/hw/mamba_kernel_mirror.py) is independent for mirror-vs-oracle but has a DEGRADED structural coverage worth flagging (not a co-wrong): unlike decoder/vit it has no top-level _recompute_layer — it reads per-layer intermediates from its own forward cache rather than recomputing them at the top level (it does recompute fwd state inside the scan backward, lines 134/145/360). This means it cannot detect smem-aliasing dead-buffer-read bugs in the backward that overwrite a cached intermediate before it is read. This is an acknowledged limitation, not oracle/kernel co-derivation.
synth.notes:
All three CONFIRMED findings verified line-by-line against canonical sources and hold (real=true): SG2-B1 (oracle_step mirrors the kernel's low-rank CSA indexer instead of the canonical full-rank path; the only divergence-detecting probe is non-voting), SG11-cold-gate-blind (CI runs only the cold step-1 test whose gate is hard-pinned to 0.5 by m0=0 and whose gate-dependent surfaces are sub-tolerance; the discriminating warm-up gate is CLI-only and never run by pytest/CI; the advertised test_sg11_gate_warmup_catches_momentum_bug has no definition), and sg11-gate-oracle-is-local-twin (two same-file twins both hardcode the `momentum` operand with no external/canonical anchor — and the docstring-referenced anchors sg11_gate_ref/_cosine_gate_ref do NOT exist anywhere in the repo, so the latent operand-swap shape is real and the fix must be the literal-anchored closed-form case, option (a)).

SYSTEMATIC PREVENTION of oracle/kernel co-derivation (the SG11 co-wrong failure mode):
1. ANCHOR DIRECTION RULE: every oracle's expected value must be derived from the canonical ALGORITHM source (csrc/algorithms/*.h, grokking_optimizers/optimizers/*.py) — never from a re-statement of what the kernel does. When a kernel deliberately diverges from canonical (e.g. SG2 low-rank vs full-rank), the divergence must be gated by an explicit, VOTING tolerance/expected-set test, not merely printed.
2. NO TWO SAME-FILE TWINS: an fp64 'oracle' and an fp32 'mirror' that differ only in precision/reduction shape and live in the same file are not independent — they fall to a single co-edit. Pin every load-bearing operand/index/normalization from ONE non-twin canonical source (a real shared ref, or a literal hand-computed case), so the oracle and the thing-under-test cannot be edited in lockstep.
3. OPERAND-DISCRIMINATION TEST: for any cosine/dot/selection where the operand identity matters, include a closed-form case where the correct operand and the plausible-wrong operand give DIFFERENT answers, and assert equality to the former AND inequality to the latter — so an operand swap fails by construction (catches the exact SG11 class). Same idea for top-k: assert selected indices, not just scores.
4. LIVENESS = CI-COLLECTED: a discriminating instrument that exists only behind a CLI flag or in an uncollected function is not a guard. Every regression-class test must be reachable by the exact CI command (pytest -m hw here), and must be NON-VACUOUS — assert the discriminating quantity is actually exercised (e.g. gate_div>1e-4, momentum nonzero) and that the gate-dependent surface is load-bearing (pump rescale so the term is above tolerance) rather than damped below the parity tol.
5. NO SILENT REPORTS: any probe that surfaces a known divergence must set an _ok flag that participates in the gate's boolean verdict; `if verbose: print(...)` is documentation, not a gate.
6. PHANTOM-REF GUARD: docstrings that point at anchor functions (sg11_gate_ref, _cosine_gate_ref) must reference functions that EXIST; a CI lint that greps for the named anchors would have caught that these are phantoms."
